title: Men’s 1,500-meter freestyle world record demolished by Germany’s Johannes Liebmann at Euros
content:
Johannes Liebmann of Germany smashed the men’s 1,500-meter freestyle world record on Saturday at the European Aquatics Championships in Paris, swimming the longest pool race in 14 minutes, 26.79 seconds to beat the old mark by nearly four seconds.

American Bobby Finke had held the record since the 2024 Olympics, when he swam 14:30.67 to win gold, also in Paris.

The 19-year-old Liebmann jumped out fast and was ahead of Finke’s pace the entire time. The only question was whether he could keep it up in the latter stages of the distance race. At nearly every split, he extended his lead on Finke’s time, leading it by five seconds heading into the final 50 meters.

Liebmann outpaced Hungary’s Zalán Sarkany, who finished in second, by over 60 meters and nearly 13 seconds. Sarkany competed collegiately at Indiana, was an eight-time All-American, and broke the NCAA record in the 1,000-yard freestyle earlier this year.

Earlier this week, Liebmann also won gold in the 800-meter freestyle earlier, setting a European record of 7:37.59. It was a record Liebmann himself previously held.
